chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī (may Allah be pleased with him) says in a long hadith:

His words (peace be upon him): 'fa aṭa’u dhikrahu' constitute the highest forms of brevity and eloquence. He means to say that he was being given news about the Prophet from the commencement of his setting out till he reached this place, and he has expressed this sense in this wonderful expression.

key_terms.فَأَطَأُ ذِكْرَهُ: Fa aṭa’u dhikrahu (a concise phrase meaning 'I would tread upon his mention' or 'convey his news')

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'fa aṭa’u dhikrahu' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī interprets the phrase 'fa aṭa’u dhikrahu' as a masterful example of eloquence and brevity, indicating that the Prophet’s news was continuously transmitted to him from the beginning of his journey until his arrival. This interpretation highlights the linguistic precision of the Imams, where a single metaphorical expression encapsulates a prolonged period of ongoing communication, reflecting the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt in receiving and preserving divine guidance.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Amīr al-mu’minīn’s words “fa aṭa’u dhikrahu” constitute the highest forms of brevity and eloquence. He means to say that he was being given news about the Prophet from the commencement of his setting out till he reached this place, and he has expressed this sense in this wonderful expression.
